sections.text: Yellow perch and walleye fishing remained very slow. Heavy rain and high winds restricted angler access and degraded water clarity across the lake, while a harmful algae bloom continued to spread. Yellow perch catch rates were reportedly very low. However, anglers targeting smallmouth and largemouth bass in local channels experienced strong results using soft plastics, particularly in areas north of Lake Erie Metropark.
Over the past week, fishing was very slow, with only a few yellow perch caught on the east side of Spoils Island in 15 feet of water.

Fishing was generally slow due to high winds across all areas. A few yellow perch were caught near the Spark Plug mark in the shipping channel midweek. Boat anglers also caught a few largemouth bass over the weekend in Sunset Marina while casting various artificial baits.

Boat anglers caught a few mature Chinook salmon while trolling in the basin and off the breakwalls. Glow and chrome/red-head plugs were most effective. Pier anglers also landed a few Chinook salmon while casting glow spoons.

Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught 35 to 90 feet down in 100 to 170 feet of water. Orange and green spoons as well as green flies were effective. A few Chinook salmon were caught off the pierheads on glow plugs, while pier anglers landed a few salmon casting spoons.
Pier fishing remained decent. Most Chinook and coho salmon were caught by anglers casting spoons and spinners. Boat anglers experienced slower fishing, with most boats staying near the piers.

Pier fishing was fair, with anglers catching a decent number of Chinook salmon on crankbaits. Fishing pressure remained high. Boat anglers caught a few salmon while trolling the pierheads, and the anglers fishing in approximately 100 feet of water had good mixed-bag catches.

Boat anglers fishing the lower river caught a few salmon, though fishing was generally slow. Fishing conditions near the Berrien Springs Dam were similar, with anglers catching a few salmon amidst overall slow activity.
Shore anglers caught Chinook salmon and coho salmon while casting spoons. A few fish were also taken by anglers trolling.

Fishing remained slow overall, and windy weather kept boat anglers off the water. Anglers fishing from the pier in Tawas caught rock bass, largemouth bass, and an occasional walleye. A few salmon were caught out of the Tawas River, while channel catfish and an occasional walleye were landed in the Au Gres River.

High winds hampered angler effort over the past week. When anglers were able to get out, a mixed bag of Chinook salmon, Atlantic salmon, walleye, and occasional steelhead was caught. The best results were in 30 to 50 feet of water throughout Thunder Bay. Spoons in a variety of colors were productive throughout the water column.

Anglers had success targeting Chinook salmon while drifting spawn and beads near the 9th Street Dam throughout the day. Casting stickbaits and spoons was also productive in the evening and after dark. Boat anglers had some success trolling deep-diving crankbaits and spoons. A few Atlantic salmon and coho salmon were taken as well.

Anglers at the Cheboygan Dam spillway primarily caught Chinook salmon, along with an occasional coho salmon, pink salmon, or steelhead. Catch rates varied daily. Rain early in the week brought a fair push of salmon to the dam, where anglers caught up to three salmon per day. The bite slowed significantly as the week progressed, with weekend anglers averaging fewer than one fish per trip. Salmon and trout were taken on cast small spoons and minnow-style crankbaits, as well as drifted or bottom-bounced beads and spawn. Small walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass were also caught between the Cheboygan Dam and the State Street drawbridge while floating nightcrawlers.

Adult chinook salmon were present in good numbers in 20 to 30 feet of water off Swan Bay, though the bite was late. Anglers trolled plugs and body baits off planer boards. Outside the bay, up the lake, and straight out from the harbor, anglers caught lake trout, immature Chinook salmon, and an occasional steelhead, coho salmon, or walleye. Successful anglers ran lines throughout the water column near baitfish. Spoons in standard and slim sizes were the most effective lures. Productive colors included white, green, blue, orange, yellow, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Angling effort was light due to rough, windy weather. When anglers were able to get out, lake trout were caught off Stoneport and between the lighthouses. An occasional Chinook salmon was also caught off Stoneport, False Presque Isle, and off the Grand River outlet north of the marina. Steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye were caught on occasion. The most productive depths were 45 to 80 feet of water, with lines run throughout the water column. Anglers fished a mix of J-plugs and spoons in white, green, blue, orange, and glow patterns early in the morning and late in the day.

Pier fishing remained slow, with very few Chinook salmon reported over the weekend. Anglers caught a small number of Chinook salmon from the pier using spoons and jigging spoons. On Lake Michigan, anglers targeting Chinook salmon found fish in 90 to 250 feet of water while trolling 40 to 80 feet down with plugs and spoons, along with a few coho salmon and steelhead in the mix. Anglers also reported a few salmon from the channel and Manistee Lake, as well as northern pike and smallmouth bass.

Pier fishing remained very slow. Anglers trolling for Chinook salmon off Big Sable Point caught fish in 140 to 170 feet of water while running plugs 45 to 80 feet down. Most salmon were scattered throughout the water column.

Boat anglers targeting salmon reported low catch numbers despite marking a decent number of fish. Water temperature rose, holding around 80 feet down. Anglers targeting salmon near Medusa Creek reported slow action while trolling and drifting skein.

Anglers targeting salmon in the Bear River reported salmon and an occasional steelhead while fishing beads, flies, and skein. Anglers fishing off the piers and breakwall in Petoskey reported slow but steady action casting spoons in the early morning. Boat anglers trolled primarily in 30 feet of water or less using plugs and body baits. The thermocline was reported around 80 feet down.

Anglers fishing out of Elk Rapids caught lake trout while trolling 80 feet down in 110 to 140 feet of water. A few ciscoes were also caught, with most caught higher in the water column around 45 feet down. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught mixed bags of lake trout, cisco, and salmon while trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water.

Boat activity was minimal. Anglers targeted Chinook salmon on the first bank with little success. Water temperatures near the harbor pierhead were in the low 60s, with a few salmon entering the harbor. Pier anglers had the best success catching Chinook salmon before sunrise while floating skein.

Mature Chinook salmon were still landed out front and off the shelf in 120 to 160 feet of water, but overall numbers remained low due to warm water temperatures. Anglers jigging as well as pier anglers reported low catch numbers, as most Chinook salmon moved into the Betsie River. In Platte Bay, coho salmon fishing was moderate for anglers jigging skein near the bottom.

Boat anglers began targeting yellow perch in Suttons Bay, Omena Bay, and Northport. A few anglers had successful trips when using natural bait. Lake trout anglers were trolling near Ballenger Creek in depths ranging from 80 to 120 feet of water.

Walleye fishing was fair to good. Anglers caught fish casting jigs tipped with live bait or artificial bait featuring glow paint, using erratic, darting presentations to trigger strikes. Anglers trolling reported success using crawler harnesses or slender diving baits. Yellow perch fishing yielded mixed results with some anglers near the Escanaba River and harbor having successful outings, locating schools remained difficult. Minnows fished along deep-water structures and flats produced the best results. Coho salmon were frequently observed, but action was generally slow. Trolling artificial lures such as spoons and crankbaits yielded little success, and anglers using forward-facing sonar while jigging also encountered a tough bite. Early morning and low-light periods near or after dark offered the best opportunity for coho salmon.

Boat anglers reported catching a few coho salmon and splake while trolling the bay. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River also caught splake and a few coho salmon. Spawn and spinners were the most effective baits.

Over the past week, the river saw minimal angling effort. Anglers reported low catches of walleye, primarily caught by jigging. Trolling proved largely ineffective. Inclement weather throughout the week hindered overall fishing conditions.

The access sites at Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay each saw low angling effort over the past week. High winds and frequent rain showers continued to limit lake access on multiple days. However, fair-weather days produced good fishing, with anglers reporting solid catches of lake trout along with lesser numbers of coho salmon. Fish were taken by trolling across depths ranging from 40 to 150 feet.

The harbor saw low angling effort over the past week due to inclement weather limiting lake access. When conditions allowed, anglers reported mixed catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout in low to fair numbers. Lake trout comprised most of these catches. Fish were taken by trolling in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet.

Following early-week rain, some additional Chinook salmon moved into the Carp River and the mouth of Nunns Creek. Anglers caught up to two fish per trip when casting small spoons and minnow-style crankbaits, or drifting spawn. The bite slowed heading into the weekend, with anglers experiencing low success rates despite significant effort. Pink salmon were reported in the rapids upstream of the Carp River fishing pier near the river mouth.
Fishing activity was slow, though boat anglers reported success targeting lake trout when jigging and trolling. Anglers fishing off the breakwall reported a slow salmon bite.

River anglers reported catching pink salmon and Chinook salmon. A small run of Chinook salmon entered the river, with fish observed near the mouth and up near the dam. Anglers trolling and casting crankbaits downstream of the paper mill and rapids reported occasional catches, though Chinook salmon fishing was slower overall. Shore anglers landed a few fish drifting skein, egg sacs, and beads, while other anglers caught fish casting shallow-running crankbaits during low-light periods at dusk and into the night.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, primarily near the bottom using downriggers. A few anglers trolling near the mouth of the Chocolay and Carp rivers from Lower Harbor caught coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and brown trout at depths around 30 feet in 60 feet of water. Catch rates appeared to increase as water temperatures cooled.

Angler participation increased out of Au Train on calm weather days. Lake trout fishing was productive, with several angler limits. Trolling near the bottom in 140 to 180 feet of water out toward the Flats northeast of Au Train Island yielded steady success. Anglers jigging near the bottom off Au Train Island in 40 to 80 feet of water landed lean lake trout weighing 7 to 10 pounds. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in 40 to 60 feet of water marked numerous fish on electronics, though no catches were reported. Activity near river mouths and Scott Falls is expected to increase over the coming weeks as water temperatures cool.

Anglers reported fair fishing, with catches consisting of coho salmon, lake trout, and splake, along with a few larger Chinook salmon taken by trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations. Anglers jigging for lake trout experienced fair action using both natural and artificial presentations in 100 to 140 feet of water. Shore fishing remained slow, though anglers casting from shore managed to catch a few coho salmon. Lake Independence, Big Bay: Fishing activity slowed, with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers had the best success jigging in 15 to 20 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good lake trout fishing while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. A few coho salmon and steelhead were also caught while trolling, though overall numbers remained low. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported good action when using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers in the Les Cheneaux area caught yellow perch in the Cedarville and Government Bay areas, sorting through smaller fish to keep a full limit. Very few splake were present in the Hessel area. Smallmouth bass fishing was good around the islands near Hessel. In DeTour, when weather permitted, anglers had good success trolling for lake trout on the flats while also taking a few pink salmon.

High winds this week left the water murky, and algae blooms were reported moving out of the River Raisin. Surface water temperatures remained above 70 degrees. Fishing for both walleye and yellow perch was slow on the Michigan side. Yellow perch did not yet show up in large numbers, with catches dominated by smaller fish rather than keeper-sized perch. The three main areas off Stony Point, the River Raisin, and Luna Pier produced similar results. Walleye were found primarily in deeper water on the Ohio side. Smallmouth bass and largemouth bass fishing was productive, with underspin jigs fished around submerged cover yielding the best action.

Yellow perch fishing was hit or miss. When fish were biting, anglers caught high numbers of 5- to 7-inch yellow perch alongside an occasional 9- to 11-inch keeper, averaging 10 to 15 kept fish per boat. Most angling effort was concentrated around buoys A, B, C, 1, and 2. Walleye fishing remained very slow.
High winds kept anglers off the bay for most of the weekend. A few yellow perch were caught mid-week off Fish Point in 17 feet of water, but overall fishing remained slow.
Boat anglers caught salmon from the breakwalls out in 80 feet of water. Glow spoons and plugs had the most success.

A mix of coho salmon and Chinook salmon were caught from the pierheads out to 90 feet of water. Glow plugs, glow spoons, and green flies were all productive. Pier anglers caught both Chinook salmon and coho salmon on glow spoons, while largemouth bass were caught on drop-shot rigs.

Boat anglers caught a few salmon, but overall fishing remained slow. Pier fishing was also slow, though a few salmon moved into the river. A few steelhead were caught on shrimp, but overall fishing was slow. Yellow perch fishing was also slow.

Boat anglers experienced good fishing in around 100 feet of water. Boat anglers also caught a few salmon around the pierheads as well as in 40 feet of water. Pier fishing pressure was very high. Anglers caught coho salmon and Chinook salmon in the mornings and at dusk, with most fish taken by casting spoons. Yellow perch fishing slowed slightly, though a few fish were caught in 38 feet of water.
There were a few salmon in the lower river. Anglers also caught some fish at the Berrien Springs dam.
Anglers who fished the black river caught a few salmon. Most of the fish were caught when trolling the river.
Anglers fishing worms under bobbers reported success targeting panfish.
Panfish were abundant across most local lakes, and smallmouth bass action was strong on the Kalamazoo River following recent storms.

While a growing number of anglers targeted salmon, fishing remained slow. A handful of Chinook salmon were caught on J-plugs and spoons while trolling from the pierhead into the shipping channel. A few walleye were also taken in depths of 25 to 40 feet of water in those same areas. High winds hampered angler activity. Pier anglers reported only a few Chinook salmon caught on glow spoons during early morning and late evening hours.

Only a few salmon were caught by anglers near the 9th Street Dam while drifting eggs and beads. White and green crankbaits also produced a few fish late in the evening. Anglers casting orange, gold, and green spinners reported catching smallmouth bass near the Holiday Inn. Trolling the river for Chinook salmon yielded slow action.

High winds kept angler activity low. Anglers who ventured out reported good lake trout fishing in 50 to 80 feet of water. Flasher and Spin-A-Lure combinations as well as spoons were productive in the bottom half of the water column. Walleye anglers experienced some success trolling crankbaits 10 to 20 feet down in 30 to 40 feet of water. A few steelhead were also caught on brightly colored spoons fished in the top 20 feet. Shore anglers reported no success targeting salmon or bass.

High water temperatures in the Cheboygan River limited salmon activity over the past week, with many fish dropping back into Lake Huron in search of cooler water. Shore anglers occasionally caught Chinook salmon or steelhead while bottom-bouncing beads or casting minnow-style crankbaits. Spoons were less effective but still produced fish. Anglers fishing the Cheboygan Dam spillway and pier reported similar results, with the best success occurring during low-light periods before daybreak and after sunset. Boat anglers trolling the mouth of the river worked hard for fish, with flasher-fly combinations and J-Plugs producing the best results. Anglers floating nightcrawlers in the lower river caught walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass.

Anglers casting spoons, spinners, and body baits off the pier caught a few Chinook and coho salmon early in the morning and at dusk. Pink, orange, and blue/silver were effective colors for spoons and spinners, while clown and fire tiger patterns worked best for body baits. A few walleye were also caught off the pier. Boat anglers trolling spoons and plugs in 15 to 30 feet of water off the pierhead caught Chinook salmon and coho salmon, while trolling in 70 to 120 feet of water produced lake trout.

Anglers trolling spoons in 60 to 85 feet of water caught a few steelhead. Lake trout were caught in 70 to 120 feet of water by anglers trolling spoons and Spin-N-Glos in the bottom 10 to 30 feet of the water column. A few Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught in the harbor by anglers casting spinners, spoons, and body baits.

Mature Chinook salmon staged off Swan Bay. Anglers targeted them inside 45 feet of water, trolling J-plugs and Bombers very early or very late in the day. Anglers targeting juvenile Chinook salmon, steelhead, lake trout, coho salmon, and walleye fished in 45 to 90 feet of water. Locate baitfish to find the most productive areas and deploy lines throughout the water column for best results. Standard and slim-profile spoons were effective. Productive colors included green, orange, blue, white, and UV glow patterns during low-light hours. Anglers reported success trolling straight out from the marina south toward Swan Bay and Adams Point, or north toward 40 Mile Point.

A mixed bag of Chinook salmon, steelhead, and lake trout, along with an occasional walleye and coho salmon, were caught over the past week. A few Chinook salmon were caught south toward Stoneport and between the lighthouses. The most productive depths were 45 to 90 feet of water, with lines set throughout the water column for best results. Spoons were the most effective bait, with both standard-size and slim profiles yielding fish. Productive colors included orange, green, blue, white, and UV glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.
Anglers targeting Chinook salmon found fish in deep water past the shelf in 140 to 150 feet of water, trolling 80 to over 100 feet down with plugs and flasher-fly combinations. Pier fishing was slow.
Pier fishing was slow. Most of the boat activity was in evening with many anglers reporting slow fishing.

Anglers reported warm water temperatures with limited success over the past week. Anglers who found success caught salmon 100 to 125 feet down in 125 to 150 feet of water. Anglers fishing near the Medusa cement plant shoreline reported a few fish moving into shallow water.

Boat anglers reported warm water temperatures with no distinct thermocline until reaching depths greater than 100 feet of water. Anglers fishing the Bear River reported an occasional Chinook salmon and small steelhead moving into the system. Drifting beads and flies produced fair results.

High winds limited fishing activity over the past week. Anglers trolling near the mouth of the Boardman River caught salmon in 90 to 130 feet of water using spoons and plugs. A few lake trout were caught by anglers trolling the West Bank in 120 to 150 feet of water. In the Boardman River, anglers drifting skein reported taking a few salmon.

Windy conditions kept fishing effort low. Boat anglers were limited to fishing the first bank, where water temperatures were reported at 68 degrees. Anglers trolling in 150 to 200 feet of water set baits 90 to 100 feet down, though catches along the first bank shelf were low. A few Chinook salmon moved into the harbor.

Fishing effort was very low. Anglers targeting lake trout had successful trips while trolling throughout Suttons Bay and jigging near Stony Point. Chinook salmon were observed swimming near the Northport pierheads.
Panfish fishing was good on all the lakes with multiple anglers catching limits of very large bluegills from shore and on the water.
Fishing for bass and panfish was very good. Multiple anglers reported good bass fishing after sun rise in the morning. Some limits of good bluegill were also caught.
Walleye fishing was good in the late evening.
Anglers reported success catching smallmouth bass on the Muskegon River downstream from Croton Dam. Chinook salmon were not yet reported on the Muskegon River due to warm water temperatures.

Lake Michigan was productive, with anglers catching near limits of Chinook salmon in 100 to 140 feet of water. Increased water temperatures slowed the movement of Chinook salmon into the rivers. Chinook salmon did not push up the White River due to warm water temperatures.

Anglers targeting walleye reported fair to good fishing over the past week. In lower Little Bay de Noc, anglers found fish around deep structure, including points and humps. In the upper bay, anglers reported success along weed edges and the eastern shoreline. Casting anglers caught fish using artificial reaction baits retrieved near the bottom with a fast-snapping motion, tied to braided line with a clear leader. Anglers trolling or drifting ran crawler harnesses or crankbaits, while a few jigging live bait on jigheads reported limited success. Yellow perch fishing was generally slow near the Escanaba River and in the upper bay. Anglers reported inconsistent catches near the Escanaba harbor due to shifting winds. Anglers targeting coho salmon near the Escanaba River reported active bite windows, catching fish in the river and near the mouth. Anglers trolling near the river mouth had the best success with brightly colored crankbaits, while casting spoons produced limited results.

Weather conditions limited fishing activity for boat anglers over the past week. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River reported a slow bite, catching only a few splake and coho salmon. Successful baits included spawn and spinners.

Anglers reported slow overall fishing effort on the river over the past week. Anglers jigging caught fair-to-low numbers of walleye, while trolling remained less effective. Heavy rain throughout the week created poor fishing conditions.

Angling effort from Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay decreased over the past week due to high winds and rain limiting lake access. Anglers trolling in depths ranging from 40 to 150 feet of water caught lake trout and coho salmon in low-to-fair numbers.

Angling effort in the harbor decreased over the past week as high winds and rain limited lake access. Anglers trolling in 40 to 150 feet of water reported low-to-fair catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout.

Anglers spent considerable time targeting salmon over the past week as water temperatures remained in the high 60s. Wading anglers at the mouth of Nunns Creek caught fish on spoons and spawn, while anglers casting minnow-style crankbaits off the footing pier near the mouth of the Carp River had the best results. The most productive fishing occurred before daybreak and after sunset, particularly with glow lures. Water temperatures dropped into the high 50s by the end of the week.
Fishing activity was low due to weather conditions. Anglers fishing off the breakwall had little luck targeting coho salmon.

Anglers reported slow-to-fair Chinook salmon fishing in the river. Anglers reported seeing pink salmon and Chinook salmon in the river, but overall catch rates were low. Anglers anticipated a fresh push of salmon after warm, dry conditions over the past week. Anglers caught fish using crankbaits and by drifting skein and other spawn presentations.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks toward Granite Island and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, primarily near the bottom on downriggers. A few anglers trolling out of Lower Harbor caught Chinook salmon and brown trout at depths around 30 feet down in 60 feet of water. Anglers fishing the Carp and Chocolay rivers reported catching Coho salmon and brown trout as fish began moving into the tributaries.

Angler effort increased out of Au Train on days with favorable winds. Following low fishing pressure over the summer, catch rates improved. Anglers continued finding lake trout in 140 to 180 feet of water near the flats northeast of Au Train Island and west of Wood Island Reef, with most fish caught near the bottom. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in 40 to 60 feet of water marked numerous fish, though few strikes were reported. Activity is expected to increase over the next several weeks as salmon and trout move toward river mouths, with the waters off Scott Falls and local tributaries offering the best opportunities.

Anglers reported poor to fair fishing, with catches consisting mostly of lake trout. Coho salmon and splake were taken in small numbers, alongside a few larger Chinook salmon caught by anglers trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations. Anglers jigging in depths around 200 feet of water reported a fair bite for lake trout when using both natural and artificial baits. Shore fishing remained slow. Lake Independence, Big Bay: Fishing activity increased with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers did best when trolling in 10 to 15 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported good fishing for lake trout while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. A few Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught while trolling, though numbers remained very low. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite on natural baits in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers caught lake trout while trolling and jigging out of the West and Middle entrances in the Les Cheneaux Islands. Anglers also caught a few yellow perch in the Hessel Marina and off Island 8. Northern pike catches were common in Hessel, though most fish were small. Smallmouth bass fishing was good for anglers casting around rock piles. In DeTour, anglers caught a few pink salmon but mostly caught lake trout while trolling through the Flats.
Anglers found a high success rate for lake trout near Au Train Bay.
Few salmon were caught in the river.

Unfortunately the weather did not really cooperate and it made for a tough couple of days of fishing. Early in the week we had some cloudy weather which made for a good iso bite…

The flooding and worm flow events shuffled the deck and gorged the fish. I spent a significant amount of time searching water for rising fish…

Most of our rivers have just returned to normal levels or slightly higher than normal depending on where you are at. There is rain in the forecast so I would expect…
